title: Cinema Ticket Desk
brief: Work the ticket desk. Your program asks for a name, an age and a day number, then decides the ticket category and price, names the day, and adds a weekend surcharge to everyone who is actually paying. Every decision tool from this module gets used once.

problem.goal: Ask for a name, an age and a day number (1 to 7). Print the customer's name, the day name, the age category, the base price, whether it is a weekend, and the total price.
rules: Categories by age: under 5 is Infant and free, under 13 is Child at 120, under 60 is Adult at 250, and 60 or over is Senior at 100.
Day names come from the day number: 1 is Monday through to 7 is Sunday. Use a switch, not a chain of ifs.
The weekend surcharge is 50, and it is added only when the base price is more than 0. A free infant ticket stays free at the weekend.
Ask for the name first with nextLine(), then the two numbers with nextInt().

steps: The three questions are already written for you. Check which reading method each one uses and why the name comes first.
Use an if and else if chain on the age to set two things at once: a String for the category and an int for the base price. End it with a plain else so every age is covered.
Use a switch on the day number to get the day name. The arrow form is the tidiest, and it needs no breaks.
Make a boolean for weekend: true when the day is 6 or 7.
Work out the total. Start from the base price, then add 50 only when the price is above 0 and it is a weekend.
Print the six lines exactly as in the example, then press Check Project.
hints: Press Run before changing anything. It asks three questions and prints one line. Answer Amara, 10, 6 to match the example while you build the rest.

Declare the two variables above the chain so they still exist after it: `String category;` and `int basePrice;` with no value yet. Each branch then assigns both. Java will tell you if you miss a branch.

Order the age tests from the smallest band upwards: under 5, then under 13, then under 60, then a plain `else` for everyone older. A chain stops at the first true test, so you never need to write `age >= 5 && age < 13`.
For the day, the arrow switch that produces a value is ideal: `String dayName = switch (day) { case 1 -> "Monday"; ... default -> "Unknown"; };` Do not forget the semicolon after the closing brace.
The weekend test is one line and needs no if: `boolean weekend = day == 6 || day == 7;`
For the total, start with `int total = basePrice;` then guard the surcharge: `if (basePrice > 0 && weekend) { total += 50; }`. That guard is what keeps a free infant ticket free.
The remaining prints all follow the model line, for example `System.out.println("Base price: " + basePrice);` and `System.out.println("Total: " + total);`
inputHint: Your program asks 3 questions, so type 3 answers: a name, then an age, then a day number from 1 to 7.

tests.name: A child on a Saturday pays the surcharge
An adult on a Wednesday pays the base price
A free infant ticket stays free at the weekend

successMessage: The ticket desk is open! 🎬 You used a chain for the age bands, a switch for the day, a guarded if for the surcharge and comparisons for the weekend, and every one of the four cases came out right, including the tricky free ticket on a Sunday. Next module you learn to repeat work with loops, and your programs stop running once and stopping.
